title: Representing pair in coherent curve duality
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and let $C$ be a $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme] with its specified structure morphism $f:C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. For $p\geq 0$ define $H^p_k(C,-)$ to be the module cohomology functor of [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology], with scalars restricted from $\Gamma(C,\mathcal O_C)$ to $k$ along the ring map induced by $f$. A representing dualizing pair on $C$ consists of a sheaf of $\mathcal O_C$-modules $\omega$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], a proof that $\omega$ is coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and for every coherent sheaf of $\mathcal O_C$-modules $F$ a $k$-linear isomorphism $e_F:\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_C}(F,\omega)\simeq\operatorname{Hom}_k(H^1_k(C,F),k)$. These isomorphisms are required to be natural contravariantly in coherent $F$: for every morphism $a:F\to G$ of coherent modules and $b:G\to\omega$, $e_F(b\circ a)=e_G(b)\circ H^1_k(C,a)$. This defines the data of a representing pair; it asserts no existence on an arbitrary $k$-scheme and imposes no connectedness condition.
